title: Square-root bound for binary Hayes population refinements
statement: Let ell >= 200, let n be 2 ell + 1 or 2 ell + 2, and let N_j(b) be the level-j quotient population obtained by aggregating the degree-n Mangoldt populations in E_ell. For every 1 <= j <= ell and every level-(j-1) parent b, the absolute difference between its two level-j child populations is at most 3 j times 2^ceil((n-j)/2).

provenance.source: Axeyum gf2-lemire lane; exact raw-population Haar refinement of the binary Hayes class distribution

notes: This is a uniform analytic obligation, not a finite computation result. The CAS reconstructs every finite leaf population from the signed sibling differences and checks that the displayed bound implies the desired endpoint discrepancy: the symbolic triangle closes the odd endpoint from ell=13 and the even endpoint from ell=15. Both endpoint rows satisfy the exact triangle for every tested ell from 16 through 20. The sharper coefficient-two version is false at (ell,n,j)=(19,40,4): 2112512 exceeds 2097152. The coefficient-three version survives the tested rows, but finite survival does not establish ell>=200. Unlike the previously refuted valuationwise square-root claim, each sibling population here already aggregates the complete Mangoldt class population at its quotient level. No proof operation is registered.
